Printed pages 72–73. Table header reads: "EXPENDITURE / Figures / Title / Heading / 2027 appropriations (Commitments, Payments) / 2026 appropriations (Commitments, Payments) / 2025 out-turn (Commitments, Payments)".
Figures are in EUR. 2027 and 2026 columns are whole euro; 2025 out-turn carries decimal centimes.

Layer 2 — CHAPTER 01 01 structure and CHAPTER 01 02 legal basis

C0101-001 — Chapter 01 01 legal-basis pointer
FILE: SEC03.pdf LOCATION: Chapter 01 01, "Legal basis" block, printed p. 74 QUOTE: "Legal basis / See Chapter 01 02." NAMES: NO PUBLICATION NAMED — cross-reference only TENSE: PRESENT NOTES: The support-administrative chapter states no legal basis of its own and points to the operational chapter. C0101-002 — Article 01 01 01 subtotal
FILE: SEC03.pdf LOCATION: Chapter 01 01 table, "Article 01 01 01 — Subtotal" row, printed p. 74 QUOTE: "Article 01 01 01 — Subtotal 861 204 182 837 906 671 802 524 004,62 93,19 %" NAMES: NO PUBLICATION NAMED TENSE: N/A — figures row NOTES: Support expenditure for Horizon Europe. 2027 861 204 182; 2026 837 906 671; 2025 out-turn 802 524 004,62. C0101-003 — Item 01 01 01 01
FILE: SEC03.pdf LOCATION: Chapter 01 01 table, Item 01 01 01 01 row, printed p. 73 QUOTE: "01 01 01 01 Expenditure related to officials and temporary staff implementing Horizon Europe — Indirect research 1.0.11 188 512 961 187 011 774 167 019 148,93 88,60 %" NAMES: Horizon Europe TENSE: N/A — figures row NOTES: Carries an MFF sub-heading code, 1.0.11 — a column present in the article/item tables but not in the Title- or Chapter-level summaries. Every item row in Chapter 01 01 carries one.

C0101-004 — Item 01 01 01 01 remarks
FILE: SEC03.pdf LOCATION: Item 01 01 01 01, "Remarks" block, printed p. 75 QUOTE: "This appropriation is intended to cover expenditure relating to officials and temporary staff implementing the specific research and innovation programme — Horizon Europe and occupying posts on the authorised establishment plans engaged in indirect research actions, including officials and temporary staff posted in Union delegations." NAMES: Horizon Europe TENSE: PRESENT NOTES: "This appropriation is intended to..." is the standard opening formula for every Remarks block in this document. Names the establishment plan as the authorising instrument for the posts — the establishment plan is published within the budget itself, so it is an internal reference rather than an external terminus.

C0101-005 — Item 01 01 01 01 assigned revenue
FILE: SEC03.pdf LOCATION: Item 01 01 01 01, "Assigned revenue" block, printed pp. 75–76 QUOTE: "Assigned revenue (origin, estimated amounts and corresponding article or item of the statement of revenue). / EFTA-EEA 4 939 040 6 6 0 0 / Candidate countries and Western Balkan potential candidates 509 823 6 0 1 0" NAMES: NO PUBLICATION NAMED TENSE: PRESENT NOTES: This is a documented internal cross-reference structure worth noting for the graph: each assigned-revenue line names the revenue article or item that feeds it (6 6 0 0, 6 0 1 0) — i.e. expenditure lines in this document explicitly point back to revenue lines in Titles 6 and 6 0 of the same document. That is a stated input relationship between two parts of the same publication, running expenditure ← revenue. Whether the project treats intra-document line references as edges is a scoping question for the other end of the process; recorded here so the option exists.

"Legal basis" blocks appear 671 times in the document. These are the highest-value edge material in SEC03 — each is a named legal act with OJ reference and ELI.

p.m. entries are token lines, not zeros, and appear throughout.

Chapter 01 01 is now complete: every figures-table row, every Remarks block, every Assigned revenue block, every Legal basis block and every Reference acts block in the chapter has an entry.
Quotation convention used for repeated acts. Where a legal act's printed text at a later location is word-for-word identical to an act already quoted verbatim at an earlier entry in this batch — same title, same OJ reference, same ELI — the later entry records the location, names the act, and points at the entry holding the full quote rather than repeating it. This departs from strict one-full-quote-per-location. It was done because Items 72, 73 and 76 cite the same eleven acts in the same order with identical printed text, and Item 74 a five-act subset; quoting all 38 in full would add roughly 3,000 words of exact duplication without adding a single checkable string. Every act still carries its own citable location. If the other end of the process wants the full text at every location, the grouped entries (LB-72-01/11, LB-73-01/11, LB-74-01/05, LB-76-01/11) can be expanded mechanically from the entries they point at — flagging this so the choice is visible rather than silent.

Open discrepancies recorded, not resolved (new in this batch):
Repealed acts cited as live legal bases. All five executive-agency items cite Council Decision 2013/743/EU, whose own printed title states that it repeals Decisions 2006/971/EC, 2006/972/EC, 2006/973/EC, 2006/974/EC and 2006/975/EC — while citing those same repealed decisions as legal bases in the same block. Compounding this, batch 1 recorded at HZ-003 that Council Decision (EU) 2021/764 repeals 2013/743/EU. Three generations of specific-programme decisions therefore sit in the corpus simultaneously as stated legal bases. (LB-71-04, LB-71-05, LB-72-06 to LB-72-08)
Cross-subject legal bases, third and fourth instances. Regulation (EU) 2015/1017 (EFSI — investment guarantees) is cited as legal basis for four of the five research executive agencies, and Decision No 1230/2003/EC (Intelligent Energy — Europe, an energy programme with a stated period of 2003-2006) for four of the five. Neither is explained in the Remarks. This is the same pattern flagged in batch 1 at HZ-004 and HZ-005. (LB-71-06, LB-72-02)
Item 01 01 01 74's legal basis is narrower than its peers — five acts against eleven for Items 72, 73 and 76 — with no stated reason. (LB-74-01/05)
"Other assigned revenue" maps to two different revenue codes within one chapter: 6 0 1 0 in Article 01 01 01, 6 0 1 1 in Article 01 01 02. The label alone is not a reliable key for the expenditure ← revenue link. (C0101-041, C0101-044, C0101-065, C0101-067)
Item 01 01 02 11's Remarks block prints the same "Staff costs comprise…" sentence twice, once before and once after the direct/indirect action indents. The parallel item 01 01 01 11 prints it once. (C0101-063)
Item 01 02 02 31 (European Cybersecurity Industrial, Technology and Research Competence Centre) carries p.m. in all four appropriation columns, 0,— out-turn in both 2025 columns, and a blank execution-ratio cell — a named body with a live budget line and no appropriation in any year shown. Structural findings for the remaining extraction:
A chapter can carry more than one MFF sub-heading code. Chapter 01 01 uses 1.0.11 (Horizon Europe), 1.0.12 (Euratom) and 1.0.13 (ITER), one per article. The budget-line → MFF-heading link is therefore an article-level property in support-administrative chapters, not a chapter-level one.
The article-level legal-basis deferral targets the matching operational chapter, article by article: 01 01 01 → 01 02, 01 01 02 → 01 03, 01 01 03 → 01 04. Expect the same one-to-one mapping in the other Titles' X 01 chapters. This corrects the batch 1 reading (see CORR-001).
Executive-agency items carry a Legal basis block and the deferral pointer, not one or the other, and they are the only items in Chapter 01 01 with legal-basis blocks of their own.
A second block type exists: "Reference acts." It appears only on executive-agency items, contains exactly one Commission delegation decision each, and uses a C(YYYY) citation form with no OJ reference and no ELI — unlike every act in the Legal basis blocks. Candidate terminus material; the document does not state where these decisions are published.
Revenue codes seen so far: 5 0 4 0 (Proceeds from EURI, Title 5), 6 6 0 0 (EFTA-EEA), 6 0 1 0 (candidate countries / other countries / other assigned revenue), 6 0 1 1 (other assigned revenue, Euratom article only). Expenditure items in Title 01 therefore point back into revenue Titles 5 and 6.
Assigned-revenue composition differs by article. Article 01 01 01's blocks name EFTA-EEA, candidate countries, other countries and (on four items) EURI. Articles 01 01 02 and 01 01 03 name only "Other countries" and "Other assigned revenue". Two items — 01 01 02 01 and 01 01 02 11 — carry no assigned-revenue block at all.
The "In accordance with Articles 21, 22 and 24 of the Financial Regulation…" paragraph is chapter-level boilerplate, appearing verbatim in both Chapter 01 01 and Chapter 01 02. Expect it in every chapter; extract once per chapter with its location, do not treat recurrence as new.
Article rows can carry figures directly. Article 01 02 05 has figures and an MFF code on the article row itself, no items, no subtotal. Table-parsing that assumes figures live only on item and subtotal rows will drop it.
p.m. propagates upward as a token, not a zero. The Article 01 02 99 subtotal reproduces p.m. rather than a figure.
"99" is the completion/legacy article number in Chapter 01 02. Worth checking against other chapters.
The differentiated chapters label the ratio column "Payments (2025/2027)"; the non-differentiated chapters label it "2025/2027". A stated difference in what the printed ratio measures.

Part A — SEC09 extraction (Section IX — European Data Protection Supervisor), complete
Batch ID: SEC09-2026-08-04-A1 Strand: Finances / EU institutional budget — Section IX Governing briefs: Research.2 v2.1 (fixed) + Research.EU v0.1 (fixed) + Research.3 (amendment) Source document: SEC09.pdf — "SECTION IX — EUROPEAN DATA PROTECTION SUPERVISOR", Draft General Budget of the European Union for the financial year 2027. 31 printed pages. Scope: the whole section — Introduction, Revenue (Titles 3, 4), Expenditure (Titles 1, 2, 3, 10), Staff establishment plans S 1 and S 2. Nothing in SEC09 is left unextracted.
CONVENTION CHANGE (applies from this batch onward)
Batches A1 and A2 used one entry per table row, per Remarks block, per cited act. That does not scale: at that granularity SEC09 is ~200 entries and SEC10 ~220, for two documents that are 31 and 38 pages against SEC03's 1,114.
From this batch:
One entry per figures table, with every row quoted verbatim inside the QUOTE field in printed column order. A row remains uniquely locatable by its table plus its own printed text.
Boilerplate formulas quoted once, in a BP-nnn entry, with a complete list of every location where the identical text occurs. No location is dropped.
One entry per substantive Remarks block and per cited act, as before, where the text is not boilerplate.
This is a presentation change, not a sourcing change. Every quote is still verbatim, every location is still recorded, and the batch can be mechanically expanded back to per-row granularity. Flagging it so the choice is visible and reversible.

Layer 1 — Introduction
S09-001 — Cross-section introduction disclaimer
FILE: SEC09.pdf LOCATION: INTRODUCTION, opening paragraph (small print), printed p. 1 QUOTE: "The introduction to the budget request has been provided by each Institution together with the statement of estimate for its respective budget section. In line with Article 314§1 of the TFEU, which states that: '[…] each Institution shall […] draw up estimates of its expenditure for the following financial year. The Commission shall consolidate these estimates in a draft budget, which may contain different estimates.', the Commission has exceptionally adjusted the estimates of all Institutions. It is thus possible that figures referred to in the introduction of a specific budget section are different from those integrated into the Draft Budget." NAMES: TFEU (Article 314§1) TENSE: PRESENT NOTES: Load-bearing for the whole institutional-sections strand. The document states on its own face that each section's introduction was written by the institution, that the Commission then altered the numbers, and that the introduction may therefore contradict the tables in the same document. This is a stated authorship split inside one publication: narrative by the institution, figures by the Commission. Identical text appears at SEC10.pdf printed p. 1 (see S10-001). See S09-002 and DISC-09-01 for the consequence in this section.
S09-002 — Stated overall 2027 budget
FILE: SEC09.pdf LOCATION: INTRODUCTION, printed pp. 1–2 QUOTE: "The proposed overall budget for 2027 amounts to €32.535.000, representing an increase of 5,65%, which should be viewed in context, notably considering the new responsibilities and subsequent need for additional resources arising from the AI Act and the supervision of Large-Scale IT Systems." NAMES: AI Act TENSE: PRESENT NOTES: Note the printed thousands separator here is a full stop (€32.535.000), against the space separator used throughout the tables (30 262 189). Two number formats in one document. See DISC-09-01 for the figure discrepancy.

Structural findings:
The introduction of every institutional section is institution-authored and Commission-adjusted, and the document says so. Intro figures are not reliable against tables anywhere in Sections I–X. This should be assumed for SEC01, SEC02 and SEC04–SEC08 before they are extracted.
The MFF code series differs by section. SEC03 uses 1.0.1x; SEC09 uses 7.2.9xx (7.2.911, .912, .921, .922, .923, .931, .932, .933, .934, .941, .951, .961, .962, .974, .981, .982, .983). Ten distinct codes in a 31-page section.
Three structural variants of where figures live, all present in SEC09: on item rows (normal), on an article row with no items or subtotal (Article 2 0 0), and directly under a chapter heading with no articles or items (Chapters 10 0, 10 1).
Rows whose 2025 out-turn is 0,— or whose current figure is p.m. carry a blank execution-ratio cell, not a zero. Confirms the SEC03 finding at a second section.
"Title 3" and "Chapter 3 0" exist on both the revenue and expenditure side of the same section with unrelated content. Any index must carry a revenue/expenditure discriminator.
One institution's section can contain another body's complete administrative structure as a single chapter — the EDPB occupies Title 3 with its own buildings, staff, other-staff, staff-expenditure and operations articles, plus its own establishment plan (S 2).
The Staff Regulations and Conditions of Employment are the most-cited and least-precisely-cited instruments in the section — no OJ reference, no ELI, in every occurrence across both sections.

Open items, recorded not resolved:
The MFF sub-heading codes in SEC10 contain an unresolved placeholder character — 7.2.X11, 7.2.X12, 7.2.X31 … 7.2.X9PPPA, 7.1.2X. SEC09's equivalents are fully resolved digits. The key is not derivable from this document. Highest-priority machine-readability issue found so far. (S10-022)

(S10-015 to S10-018, S10-031, S10-012, S10-014)
Structural findings (new or confirmed at a second section):
Sections differ in budget-line granularity for identical statutory content. SEC09 puts twelve staff-cost components in one item's Remarks; SEC10 spreads the same entitlements across five items. Any cross-section comparison at item level is unsafe; only Title and Chapter totals are comparable.
Five tiers of citation precision now observable: (a) full title + OJ + ELI; (b) title + article, no OJ, no ELI (Staff Regulations, Protocol); (c) number + adopting authority, no OJ, no ELI (Decision No 111/2007); (d) adopting authority + date only (HR/VP Decision of 4 February 2014); (e) description only, no number, no date, no authority (the EP accommodation agreements, the EEAS's own Rules, Gender Action Plan III). Tiers (c) to (e) are all candidate unpublishable termini and are common in institutional sections in a way they are not in SEC03.
The closed quantified loop at Article 3 3 2 ↔ Item 3 0 0 5 is the model case for what the financial-model goal is looking for: both ends named, the amount stated identically at both, and the five downstream sibling items enumerated. Worth using as the template when scanning SEC04–SEC08.
Confirmed at a second and third section: article rows can carry figures with no items or subtotal (Article 1 4 0, Article 1 2 2, Article 2 2 4, and SEC09's Article 2 0 0); chapters can carry figures with no articles at all (Title 10 in both); blank rather than zero ratio cells where the out-turn is 0,— or the appropriation p.m.; and the revenue/expenditure "Title 3 / Chapter 3 0" numbering collision.
Establishment plans are flat in all three plans extracted so far (EDPS 78, EDPB 27, EEAS 1 750), with real internal grade movement in the EEAS plan. Introductions in both sections argue for reinforcement; the plans do not show it, and in SEC10's case that is consistent because the stated new posts are SNEs and contract agents.
Remaining in the institutional-sections strand: SEC04 (Court of Justice), SEC05 (Court of Auditors), SEC06 (European Economic and Social Committee), SEC07 (Committee of the Regions), SEC08 (European Ombudsman). None held. On the evidence of SEC09 and SEC10 each should be 25–40 pages and a single session at this convention. SEC01 and SEC02 are held at headline level only and need the same full treatment.

S07-008 — Stated execution rate and absence of reserves
FILE: SEC07.pdf LOCATION: INTRODUCTION, "2 2027 BUDGET REQUEST", printed p. 3 QUOTE: "The CoR has consistently achieved excellent annual budget outturns in recent years. The 99.9 % claim is not reconcilable with this document's own printed 2025/2027 execution-ratio column, which ranges from 38,26 % (Item 2 1 0 3) to 848,31 % (Item 2 0 0 0) — but that column has a different denominator (2027 appropriations, not 2025), so the two are not the same measure and no contradiction is asserted.

Layer 2 — Boilerplate
BP-07-01 — Article 21(3) assigned-revenue formula, revenue side
FILE: SEC07.pdf LOCATION: 8 locations, listed below QUOTE: "In accordance with Article 21(3) of the Financial Regulation, this revenue is to be considered as assigned revenue and gives rise to the entry of additional appropriations in the headings which bore the initial expenditure giving rise to the corresponding revenue." NAMES: Financial Regulation (Article 21(3)) TENSE: PRESENT NOTES: Identical text at: Article 3 1 0 Remarks (printed p. 6); Article 3 1 2 Remarks (p. 6); Item 3 2 0 2 Remarks (p. 7); Article 3 2 1 Remarks (p. 7); Article 3 2 2 Remarks (p. 7); Article 3 3 0 Remarks (p. 8); Article 3 3 3 Remarks (p. 8); Article 3 3 8 Remarks (p. 8). Eight locations. The Financial Regulation is named only as "the Financial Regulation" at every one of them — its citation number, Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509, appears exactly once in this section, at Article 4 1 9 (S07-024), and is never restated. Same naming pattern as SEC09 and SEC10; same pattern as SEC03 HZ-007.
BP-07-02 — Article 21(2) variant
FILE: SEC07.pdf LOCATION: Article 3 3 1 Remarks, printed p. 8 QUOTE: "In accordance with Article 21(2) of the Financial Regulation, this revenue is to be considered as assigned revenue and gives rise to the entry of additional appropriations in the headings which bore the initial expenditure giving rise to the corresponding revenue." NAMES: Financial Regulation (Article 21(2)) TENSE: PRESENT NOTES: One location. Identical to BP-07-01 except the sub-paragraph: 21(2) rather than 21(3), at the article for income from foundations, subsidies, gifts and bequests. SEC09 carries the same 21(2) variant at the same budget line, Article 3 3 1 (BP-09-02). Two sections, same article number, same sub-paragraph switch. SEC09 additionally carried an unqualified "Article 21" variant at Article 3 3 8 (BP-09-03); SEC07 does not — its 3 3 8 uses 21(3). So SEC07 has two variants where SEC09 had three, and the 3 3 1 → 21(2) mapping is the one both sections share.
BP-07-03 — Quantified assigned-revenue estimate, expenditure side
FILE: SEC07.pdf LOCATION: 5 locations, listed below QUOTE: "The amount of assigned revenue in accordance with Article 21(3) of the Financial Regulation is estimated at EUR [amount]." NAMES: Financial Regulation (Article 21(3)) TENSE: PRESENT NOTES: Five locations, each with its own figure: Item 1 0 0 4 — EUR 4 000 (printed p. 12); Item 1 4 0 2 — EUR 13 000 (p. 16); Item 1 4 2 0 — EUR 2 500 (p. 17); Article 2 1 6 — EUR 3 000 (p. 26); Article 2 3 2 — EUR 2 500 (p. 27). Total stated: EUR 25 000. This is the material contrast with SEC09. SEC09 declared 32 expenditure-side assigned-revenue links and quantified none of them — all 32 were p.m. (BP-09-04). SEC07 declares five and quantifies all five. SEC10 quantified 16 totalling EUR 333 636 500. So the corpus now holds three institutional sections with three different practices for the same field. None of the five SEC07 amounts names the revenue article that receives them, so unlike the SEC10 Article 3 3 2 ↔ Item 3 0 0 5 case (S10 batch close, finding 2) these do not close a quantified loop — the expenditure end is quantified and the revenue end is p.m. throughout Chapters 3 1, 3 2 and 3 3 (S07-021 to S07-024).
BP-07-04 — Provisional-appropriation transfer formula
FILE: SEC07.pdf LOCATION: 4 locations, listed below QUOTE: "This appropriation is purely provisional and may be used only after its transfer to other headings in accordance with the Financial Regulation." NAMES: Financial Regulation TENSE: PRESENT NOTES: At Article 1 4 9 (printed p. 18); Item 2 0 0 9 (p. 24); and, with "purely" absent — "This appropriation is provisional and may be used only after its transfer to other headings in accordance with the Financial Regulation." — at Article 1 2 9 (p. 14). Chapter 10 0 (p. 33) carries a fourth variant: "This appropriation is purely provisional and may be used only after transfer to other budget chapters in accordance with the Financial Regulation." — "budget chapters" rather than "headings", and no "its". Four locations, three wordings, one mechanism. Recorded because the wording differences are in the operative words (headings vs chapters) and the document does not state whether they mean different things.

DISC-07-01 — Introduction total against expenditure table
The introduction states a DB 2027 of € 142,600,414 and an increase of € 7.3 million (5.4%) over the 2026 voted budget (S07-004). The expenditure table totals 138 750 785 against a 2026 figure of 135 305 895 — an increase of 3 444 890, or 2,55 % (S07-030). Gap on the total: 3 849 629. The document supplies its own explanation at S07-001 — the institution wrote the introduction, the Commission then adjusted the figures. Recorded, not adjudicated.
DISC-07-02 — Introduction post count against establishment plan
The introduction states "498 posts in the establishment plan ( 1 new specialised cybersecurity post )" (S07-004) and the strategic guidelines state "Reinforce CoR cybersecurity with 1 AD5 post" (S07-005). The establishment plan grand total is 497 for 2027 and 497 for 2026, with AD 5 unchanged at 5 permanent posts in both years (S07-062). Gap: 1 post, and the stated grade shows no movement.
This is a materially different kind of discrepancy from DISC-07-01, DISC-09-01 and DISC-10-01, and it is worth separating. Those three are all monetary gaps between an institution-authored narrative figure and a Commission-adjusted table. This one is a headcount gap. The S07-001 disclaimer speaks only of the Commission adjusting "the estimates" — a financial term — and says nothing about establishment plans. Whether the disclaimer covers post counts is not stated anywhere in the document. Recorded as open.
DISC-07-03 — Third distinct MFF-code practice; candidate structure for the SEC10 placeholder
This is the highest-value finding in the batch and it bears directly on the corpus's highest-priority machine-readability issue (G.14 queue, finding 3).
SEC07 uses 21 distinct MFF sub-heading codes, all beginning 7.2, all with a resolved third digit of 7, plus one alphabetic form:
7.2.711, 7.2.712, 7.2.723, 7.2.731, 7.2.732, 7.2.733, 7.2.734, 7.2.741, 7.2.751, 7.2.752, 7.2.753, 7.2.761, 7.2.762, 7.2.771, 7.2.772, 7.2.773, 7.2.774, 7.2.781, 7.2.782, 7.2.783, 7.2.79SPEC
Set against the two sections already held:
SEC09 (Section IX, EDPS) — third digit 9 throughout: 7.2.911, 7.2.912, 7.2.921, 7.2.922, 7.2.923, 7.2.931 … 7.2.983. Plus 7.1.1, 7.1.2, 7.1.3.
SEC10 (Section X, EEAS) — third position X throughout: 7.2.X11, 7.2.X12, 7.2.X31 … 7.2.X83, plus 7.2.X9PPPA and 7.1.2X.
SEC07 (Section VII, CoR) — third digit 7 throughout, plus 7.2.79SPEC.
Three observations, all extraction facts:
The third character tracks the section number in each of the three sections held: Section VII → 7, Section IX → 9, Section X → X.
The final two characters form a vocabulary shared across sections — 11 (remuneration), 12 (other staff), 31/32/33/34, 51/52/53, 61/62, 71/72/73/74, 81/82/83 all appear in at least two of the three sections at comparable budget lines.
The alphabetic-suffix form is not unique to SEC10. SEC07 prints 7.2.79SPEC — a resolved third digit followed by "9" and a four-letter suffix — at four locations (Items 2 5 4 1, 2 5 4 4, 2 6 0 3 and Article 2 6 4). SEC10's 7.2.X9PPPA has the same shape: third character, then "9", then an alphabetic suffix.
What this does and does not settle. Observation 3 settles something real: SEC10's alphabetic suffix is not a corruption, a redaction or an extraction artifact, because a structurally identical form appears in a fully resolved section. The "X9…" slot is a genuine code family.
Observation 1 is a candidate reading only, and it is inference, not extraction. No document in the corpus states that the third character encodes the section number, and the reading rests on three data points. If it holds, SEC10's X is the Roman numeral for its own section number — Section X — and is not a placeholder at all, which would dissolve the problem rather than solve it. This belongs in Part B as a soft connection and must not be recorded as a resolution. Under Research.2 §5a, the useful output here is that a plausible-looking reading now exists and can be tested cheaply: SEC04, SEC05, SEC06 and SEC08 will each confirm or break it in a single glance at any chapter table. SEC06 (EESC) should be the test case, since S07-045 gives an independent reason to hold it next.
Note also that SEC07 carries no 7.1.x codes at all, where SEC09 has 7.1.1, 7.1.2 and 7.1.3. Consistent with the CoR having no pensions or European Schools lines, but the document does not say so.
Open items, recorded not resolved
Item 3 0 1 1 pension-rights citation now differs three ways across three sections — SEC09: Article 11(2) and (3). SEC10: Articles 4 and 11. SEC07: Article 11(2) and Articles 17 and 48 of Annex VIII. Same budget line, same subject, three different sets of invoked provisions, no reconciliation stated. (S07-019, S09-023, S10-017)
Item 3 0 1 2 Legal basis — present in SEC10 and SEC07, absent in SEC09. Two to one; the SEC09 batch close recorded this as open on one data point and it remains open with three. (S07-019, S09-024, S10-018)
Regulation No 260/68 name form — SEC07 prints the SEC09 form ("Regulation (EEC, Euratom, ECSC) No 260/68 of the Council"), against SEC10's inverted form. Two to one, same OJ reference, same ELI, no canonical form stated. A parallel within-document case appears at Regulation No 3518/85 (S07-039), where the Remarks and the Legal basis block on the same page print two different forms of one instrument name.
The expenditure→revenue assigned-revenue link is quantified at the expenditure end and p.m. at the revenue end. Five expenditure items state amounts totalling EUR 25 000 (BP-07-03); every revenue article that could receive them is p.m. for 2026 and 2027 (S07-013 to S07-015). No SEC07 expenditure item names the revenue article that feeds it, so unlike SEC10's Article 3 3 2 ↔ Item 3 0 0 5 case this does not close a loop. Three sections, three practices: SEC09 declares 32 links and quantifies none; SEC10 quantifies 16 totalling EUR 333 636 500 and names the counterpart article at least once; SEC07 quantifies 5 totalling EUR 25 000 and names no counterpart.
The 6,0 % standard abatement (S07-034) is applied to 58,8 % of the section's expenditure with no instrument named, no pre-abatement figure given, and no statement of where the rate is set. This is the single largest unstated arithmetic operation in the section and it stands between the establishment plan and the remuneration appropriations.
Introduction project amounts do not reconcile to table movements. Two of the nine stated new-project amounts are checkable and both fail (S07-006). Covered in direction by the S07-001 disclaimer, not in detail.
Three quantified inter-institutional flows with unnamed or unlocated counterparts — Item 3 2 0 2 receives over EUR 3,2m from "other Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies", none named (S07-014); Item 1 4 0 2 purchases interpretation from the Commission and the European Parliament with no split and no counterpart revenue line identified (S07-053); Item 1 6 3 8 contributes 700 000 to childcare facilities "operated by or approved by the institutions of the Union", none named (S07-055).
S07-045 is a candidate hard edge SEC07 → SEC06. SEC07 states a named 2026 Title 2 joint-services figure for the EESC (EUR 35 942 482) alongside its own (EUR 26 257 635). This is the first stated quantified cross-section figure in the institutional-sections strand. It is checkable only against SEC06, which is unheld. Its relationship to the introduction's 36 % claim (S07-003) is a scope difference, not necessarily a contradiction.
Under-cited instruments in SEC07 (tiers c–e)
Fifteen, comparable to SEC10's eight over a similar page count: Protocol on the privileges and immunities of the European Union (two name forms, no reference); Staff Regulations of Officials of the European Union (no reference, cited at 14 locations); Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (no reference); "the Financial Regulation" (11 locations without its number, one with); CoR Bureau decision of 9 December 2025; European Committee of the Regions decision on working regime; missions guide of the European Committee of the Regions; EP 2023 and 2024 Discharge reports; mission letters of all the European Commissioners; political guidelines for the second term of office of Commission President von der Leyen; BELE pilot project; the European Parliament pilot project behind the EU Local Councillors Network; RegHub network; 'ERASMUS for local and regional representatives' project; Conference on the Future of Europe. Plus seven named IT systems with no instrument (Sysper, EU Learn, ABAC, Ares, SUMMA, EdiT, and the Committee's own information systems) and the Translation Centre for the Bodies of the European Union.
Fully cited with OJ reference and ELI: four instruments only — Regulation (EEC, Euratom, ECSC) No 260/68, Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509, Council Regulation (ECSC, EEC, Euratom) No 3518/85, and the pair Decision 2002/620/EC and Decision 2002/621/EC.

Boilerplate entries mechanically expandable back to per-location granularity. Derived percentages and differences in NOTES fields are computed, not quoted from the source, and are the softest content in this batch.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND SEC04: the unnumbered preamble at the head of the section (S04-002) states that the Commission has 'exceptionally adjusted the estimates of all Institutions' and that 'It is thus possible that figures referred to in the introduction of a specific budget section are different from those integrated into the Draft Budget.' That is a documented, in-corpus explanation for exactly this shape of divergence: introduction figures are the Institution's own estimate, nomenclature figures are the Commission-adjusted ones. If that same preamble appears in SEC02, SEC09 and SEC10 — it is boilerplate and almost certainly does — then DISC-09-01, DISC-10-01, the SEC02 gap and this one may all be instances of one documented mechanism rather than four unexplained discrepancies. STRONG RECOMMENDATION: before writing the pattern up as a cross-section finding, check (i) whether the same preamble appears in each affected section, and (ii) whether each gap is narrative-versus-nomenclature (explained by the preamble) or headline-versus-own-sum within a single table (NOT explained by it — G.16 finding 4 describes SEC06's gap as the latter, headline total versus its own Title 1+2+10 sum, which the preamble would not account for).
